oneliner.t: Daphne minister and retired U.S. Army first sergeant who says he served 21 years and earned a Bronze Star; the only Democrat to qualify in AL-01.

upbringing.t: The public record on his early life is thin. Profiles say he served 21 years in the U.S. Army, retiring as a first sergeant, and received a Bronze Star for service in Operation Desert Storm and Operation Iraqi Freedom II. After the Army he worked in the private sector (unspecified). He is an associate minister at Macedonia Missionary Baptist Church in Daphne. His oldest son is an Army major. Birth date, birthplace and education were not found.

career.org: Alabama Arise; SEEDS (Supporting Educational Excellence in Daphne Schools, past board president)

career.role: Chair, Education, Political and Veterans Affairs Committee

platform.t: Supports federal health-care spending. Warned that letting enhanced ACA premium tax credits lapse would raise costs.
Supports banning stock trading by members of Congress, overturning Citizens United, term limits, stricter lobbying rules and a Supreme Court code of conduct.
Prioritizes affordability (health care, rent, mortgages); says Baldwin County wages lag the cost of living.
Criticizes arrest quotas that he says lead to detention of people with legal work authorization.
Says leaders deciding on war should understand the cost of deploying service members.

promises.t: Hold virtual and in-person town halls across the district whether or not Carl attends.
Push to ban congressional stock trading and overturn Citizens United.

claims.claim: 'Jerry legislated zero bills that became law in his term as a Congressman.'

record.t: A third-party tracker (The Lobby) lists 10 Carl-sponsored bills, all at 'introduced' status, which points toward accurate. Congress.gov was blocked, so the full sponsored-bill record could not be confirmed. Oct 8, 2026 re-check: The Lobby again lists 10 Carl-sponsored measures (117th and 118th Congresses), all at "introduced" with no later action. Wikipedia names no Carl-sponsored bill that became law. Both point toward the claim being accurate, but neither is a primary record (Congress.gov blocked, GovTrack errored), so the rating stays unverifiable.

claims.claim: Warned of rising health costs if the enhanced ACA premium tax credits then in place were not renewed.

said.where: campaign announcement statement quoted by Lagniappe (undated article, written before the May 19, 2026 primary, apparently late 2025)

record.t: The checkable part is that enhanced premium tax credits were in force and would lapse unless renewed. Lagniappe's own reporting says the credits were set to expire at the end of the year and cites KFF for more than 24 million Marketplace enrollees. The statute and CBO/KFF premium estimates were not opened directly, and the warning about cost increases is a forecast, so it is not rated.

claims.claim: Said estimates show a single adult in the area needs to earn well above the federal minimum wage to cover basic costs.

record.t: The article gives no figure or source. The MIT Living Wage Calculator page for Baldwin County could not be opened in this pass, so the claim was not checked against data.

research_notes: Only Democrat to qualify in AL-01 (Reflector, Aug 11, 2026). The ethics item is marked 'na': he has never held public office, so House Ethics and the Alabama Ethics Commission have no jurisdiction over his record. The Lagniappe article gives no date and refers to 'Alabama RISE' where Indivisible Mobile says 'Alabama Arise'; the latter is a known Alabama advocacy group, but the board membership itself is unverified. All bio claims come from sources relaying his own account, so they are rated unverifiable, not true. The web-search budget ran out partway through.
